documents.title: Gastroenterology Consultation Note
documents.content:
## Patient: Zara – Acute Cholecystitis

**HPI:** 67-year female presenting with acute cholecystitis, accompanied by symptomatic cholelithiasis.  Patient reports abdominal pain, localized to the right upper quadrant, radiating to the right flank.  She denies fever, chills, or nausea.

**Physical Exam:** Vital signs stable; abdominal examination reveals tenderness to palpation in the right upper quadrant. Murphy’s sign is positive.  No rebound tenderness.

**Management Plan:** Laparoscopic cholecystectomy performed to remove symptomatic gallbladder and bile duct obstruction. Post-operative pain management with analgesics as needed. Instructions provided regarding dietary restrictions and wound care. Continued monitoring for complications.

diagnostics.conclusion: Right Upper Quadrant Abdominal Ultrasound abnormal findings: Acute Cholecystitis with symptomatic cholelithiasis. Key indicators: gallbladder wall thickening, cholelithiasis.
